title: As the saying goes
goal: Recognize common proverbs and quote one at the right moment, and change only the parts of an idiom that can change.

intro.text: A proverb is a whole sentence you quote: *Damlaya damlaya göl olur*. Most use the aorist, the imperative or a `-(y)An` subject: *Gülü seven dikenine katlanır*. In many idioms the body part is the subject: *Gözüm yemedi*, I didn't dare. The possessive changes with the person; the verb stays third person.

vocab.en: not to dare (atlamaya gözüm yemedi: I didn't dare to jump)
to be a lesson (you won't forget)
not to touch (food, a thing) at all
May you be next! The same to you! (at a wedding, to the unmarried)
Congratulations! (on a birth, a homecoming or other happy news)

exercises.question: Your friend Can saves a little money every month and laughs that it's nothing. Which proverb do you answer with?

why.1: That one is about the friends who stand by you in hard times.
why.2: That one says a rumour usually has some truth in it.

exercises.explain: *Damlaya damlaya göl olur*: drop by drop, a lake forms. Small savings add up.

exercises.question: What does *Sütten ağzı yanan yoğurdu üfleyerek yer* mean?
options: People who have been hurt once become over-careful
Hot food should be eaten slowly
Milk and yogurt don't go together
Children learn from their own mistakes

why.1: The burned mouth is a picture: it's about people, not food.
why.2: The milk and yogurt are a picture, not a recipe.
why.3: The proverb is about over-caution, not learning.

exercises.explain: Whoever burned their mouth on hot milk blows even on cold yogurt: **once bitten, twice shy**. The subject is a `-(y)An` participle: *ağzı yanan*, whose mouth got burned.

exercises.en: Whoever loves the rose puts up with its thorns.
exercises.explain: *Katlanmak* (to put up with) takes the dative, and the thorn is the rose's: *diken-i-n-e*. The subject is a `-(y)An` participle: *gülü seven*, whoever loves the rose.

accept: There is no smoke without fire.
There is no smoke without a fire.
Where there is smoke, there is fire.
Where there is no fire, there is no smoke.
No smoke rises where there is no fire.
Smoke does not rise [where there is no fire|without fire|without a fire].
exercises.explain: An exact English twin. Grammar: *olmayan*, the negative `-(y)An` participle, describes *yer*: a place where there is no fire.

exercises.prompt: I was going to swim to the island, but I didn't dare.

reject.why: Here *göz* is the subject: my eye didn't eat. No accusative: *gözüm yemedi*.
The subject is *gözüm*, a noun, so the verb stays third person: *yemedi*.

exercises.explain: *Gözü yememek* (not to dare) lives in the negative. The body part is the subject, so only the possessive shows the person: *gözüm yemedi*.

exercises.text: Bu olay ___ küpe oldu; bir daha kimseye ödünç para vermem.
exercises.en: That incident taught me a lesson; I'll never lend anyone money again.

reject.why: *Kulağına* is his or her ear. The lesson is yours: *kulağıma*.
The ear needs a possessive: whose lesson is it? *kulağıma*.

exercises.hint: Whose ear? A possessive, then the dative.
exercises.explain: *Kulağına küpe olmak*: an earring in your ear, a lesson you won't forget. The possessive changes with the person; the dative stays: *kulağıma*.

exercises.gloss: to my ear (as in kulağıma küpe oldu)
exercises.explain: *Kulak* has two syllables, so its k softens before a vowel: *kulağ-*. Then `-(I)m` (my) and the dative `-(y)A`: *kulağıma*.

exercises.question: How do you say **We couldn't cope with this job**?

why.1: *Baş* takes no possessive in this idiom: *başa çıkmak*.
why.2: What you cope with takes `-(y)lA`, not the accusative: *bu işle*.

exercises.explain: In *başa çıkmak* the person is the subject and *baş* never changes; what you cope with takes `-(y)lA`.

context.tr: Ablam dün akşam doğum yaptı, bir kızı oldu!
context.en: My sister gave birth last night, she had a girl!

exercises.question: What do you say to Elif?

why.1: *Darısı başına* wishes the same luck to someone else, for instance to the unmarried at a wedding.
why.2: *Başın sağ olsun* is said after a death.
why.3: *Kolay gelsin* is for someone at work.

exercises.explain: *Gözün aydın* (your eye is bright) congratulates someone on happy news, such as a birth or a homecoming.

exercises.tr: Kızım sana söylüyorum, gelinim sen anla.
exercises.en: I'm telling you, my daughter; you understand, my daughter-in-law.
options: Kızım sana söylüyorum, gelinim sen anla.
Kızım sana söyledim, gelinim sen anla.

exercises.prompt: Boşuna dememişler: acele işe şeytan karışır.
accept: They do not say it for nothing: haste makes waste.
They did not say it for nothing: haste makes waste.
It is not for nothing that they say haste makes waste.
[As they say|They are right when they say|How true it is], haste makes waste.
[They do not say it|They did not say it] for nothing: the devil [meddles|interferes|gets involved] in hasty work.
It is not for nothing that they say the devil [meddles|interferes|gets involved] in hasty work.
[As they say|They are right when they say], the devil [meddles|interferes|gets involved] in hasty work.
exercises.explain: *Boşuna dememişler* (they didn't say it for nothing) is a common way to bring in a proverb, like *Ne demişler?* or *Atalarımız ne demiş:*.

exercises.task: Your cousin Zeynep, newly engaged, writes that her fiancé's mother criticizes her by talking to other people. Answer her in three or four sentences. Use one proverb and at least two idioms.
models: Canım Zeynep, nişanın hayırlı olsun! Galiba kayınvaliden “Kızım sana söylüyorum, gelinim sen anla.” diyor. Sen bu sözlere kulak asma; elinden geleni yapıyorsun, herkes biliyor. Gülü seven dikenine katlanır: Emre'yi seviyorsan annesiyle de başa çıkarsın.

Zeynep'ciğim, üzülme, bu herkesin başına gelir. Boşuna dememişler: damlaya damlaya göl olur; o da seni zamanla tanıyıp sevecek. Sen sözlerine kulak asma, ama ağzını da sıkı tut: kimseye bir şey anlatma.
checklist: The proverb quoted whole, perhaps brought in with *Ne demişler?* or *Boşuna dememişler*
Idioms with their cases: *sözlerine kulak asma*, *annesiyle başa çıkmak*
The possessive in the idiom follows the person: *elinden geleni*, *ağzını sıkı tut*
